authorship_disclosure: Frozen source/math expectations and this receiving adapter share an author; no original Python or candidate output generated expected answers. Runtime receiving is separate.

explicit_environment.scalar_target_assumption: IEEE754 binary64; default nearest ties-even; gradual underflow; no fast-math/reassociation/FMA contraction across source steps. Target runtime qualification remains later receiving work.
explicit_environment.context_basis: Explicit fixture configuration, not observation of a historical mutable Python process.
explicit_environment.limits_basis: Active bounded receiving configuration, not original Python acceptance limits. Core converter inputs are already constructed values; input loading is not the lexical API under test.

query_cases.title: Original QN24 texts accepted only in explicit mixed capability
query_cases.derivation: First float becomes exact Decimal then rounds at multiply; later float changes state to binary64. Old QN24 is still required under its old configuration.

query_cases.title: Flat float-state RHS asymmetry and nested restart
query_cases.derivation: Integer RHS is accepted by float arithmetic. Decimal RHS is not. A nested chain restarts its own Decimal(first) constructor and retains resulting scale.

float state division by Decimal RHS

query_cases.title: Decimal-to-float does not use decimal context precision
query_cases.derivation: Exact 9/8 needs no binary rounding; p3 Decimal arithmetic would change it, but conversion performs no Decimal arithmetic or flags.

query_cases.title: xsd:float remains binary64 and promotion is independent of family
query_cases.derivation: Both RDF float types use Python binary64. Derived integer datatype promotes through integer; result datatype follows source promotion.

query_cases.title: Unary keeps binary64 zero sign rules and defaults result dtype
query_cases.derivation: Unary applies to Python float and constructs a new Literal without requested dtype. Positive/negative zero rules are not Decimal unary rules.

runs.query:
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
SELECT ?x ?p ?m WHERE { VALUES ?x { "-0.0"^^xsd:float } BIND(+?x AS ?p) BIND(-?x AS ?m) }

query_cases.title: Float zero division enters local SPARQL domain and real consumers
query_cases.derivation: The scalar zero check raises, the source multiplicative catch creates SPARQLError, and Expr returns it. COUNT counts; SAMPLE internally retains the first error but its source projection alias Extend leaves final ?s absent. Decimal DivisionByZero trap changes only the Decimal route; float zero division still raises.

query_cases.derivation: 10^400 exceeds binary64. Multiplication first constructs Decimal integer, whose conversion permits Infinity; float Infinity*zero yields NaN without Decimal signals.

query_cases.derivation: Only additive coerces Decimal against float. These distinct fatal classes occur with no new Decimal flags.

query_cases.title: Infinity times zero distinguishes Decimal catch from float NaN
query_cases.derivation: Default Decimal InvalidOperation trap is caught only on the first path; float state ordinary arithmetic adds no Decimal signal.

query_cases.title: Float overflow and subnormal rounding are not Decimal arithmetic
query_cases.derivation: Float state overflows/underflows without Decimal flags. First float stays exact Decimal until its actual multiply and rounds p28; input lexical-to-bits is independently proved.

query_cases.title: Parser-preserved nesting exposes each binary64 rounding step
query_cases.derivation: Flat first addition rounds away one; nested subtraction is exactly -(2^53-1), so the final addition is exactly one.

query_cases.title: Same RDF retains different source-backed numeric family and scale
query_cases.derivation: Both input RDF terms are exactly identical, but one cached Python object is float and one Decimal. RDF equality/hash ignores the cache; arithmetic uses each actual cell.
